items.t: Said the Meta settlement delivers accountability and changes to make social media safer for kids and teens.
items.q: Today’s historic settlement delivers meaningful accountability and truly transformative changes to make social media safer for kids and teens

items.t: Said Vermonters and all Americans deserve better privacy protections and that more work remains to be done.
items.q: In the age of 24/7 corporate surveillance, Vermonters – and all Americans – deserve better privacy protections. I have long been a privacy advocate for Vermonters, and I believe there is work left to be done.

items.t: Said she stands up for libraries and against the executive order affecting IMLS, which she called unconstitutional.
items.q: As Vermont’s Attorney General, I am proud to stand up for our libraries and against this unconstitutional action.

record.t: Sued Meta in Chittenden Superior Court as part of a coordinated effort with 42 states.
record.q: In 2023, Attorney General Clark sued Meta in Chittenden Superior Court as part of a coordinated effort with 42 states following a bipartisan, multistate investigation.

record.t: Announced a settlement under which Meta will pay Vermont $92,700,152 to resolve a lawsuit she filed.
record.q: Meta will pay Vermont $92,700,152 to resolve the lawsuit filed by Attorney General Clark and will implement sweeping safety reforms which will fundamentally transform how the entire social media industry designs products for kids and teens.

record.t: Obtained summary judgment, with 11 other attorneys general and Pennsylvania's governor, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island.
record.q: The U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island granted a motion for summary judgment brought by Attorney General Clark and a coalition of 11 other attorneys general and the governor of Pennsylvania.

record.t: Was part of a coalition of attorneys general granted a summary judgment motion blocking Trump administration rules affecting health, education and social service programs.
record.q: Vermont Attorney General Charity Clark and a coalition of 23 other attorneys general were granted a summary judgement motion permanently blocking the Trump administration’s attempt to gut essential health, education, and social service programs for low-income families.

record.t: Joined a coalition of 20 other state attorneys general in suing the Trump administration over the dismantling of IMLS, MBDA and FMCS.
record.q: Attorney General Charity Clark today joined a coalition of 20 other state attorneys general in suing the Trump administration to stop the dismantling of three federal agencies

record.t: Joined a coalition of 24 other states and territories opposing conditions on counterterrorism funding tied to elections administration priorities.
record.q: Attorney General Charity Clark joined a coalition of 24 other states and territories opposing the Trump administration’s efforts to coerce states and local governments into advancing its elections administration priorities by withholding crucial counterterrorism funding.

record.t: Announced, with a multistate coalition, a federal court ruling in a lawsuit challenging immigration-enforcement conditions on public safety grants.
record.q: Attorney General Chairty Clark and a multistate coalition of 22 other states and districts today announced a federal judge delivered a major victory in a lawsuit challenging the federal government’s imposition of illegal immigration-enforcement conditions

record.t: Joined a bipartisan coalition of 44 other attorneys general urging Congress to pass the Senate version of the Kids Online Safety Act.
record.q: Attorney General Charity Clark today joined a bipartisan coalition of 44 other attorneys general urging Congress to pass the Senate version of the Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA)

record.t: Joined a coalition of 24 attorneys general and two governors in submitting a comment letter opposing proposed changes to the 2030 Census.
record.q: Attorney General Charity Clark today joined a coalition of 24 attorneys general and two governors in submitting a comment letter strongly opposing the Trump Administration’s proposed changes to the 2030 Census.

record.t: Was appointed co-chair of the National Association of Attorneys General's Artificial Intelligence, Internet Safety, Cyber Privacy and Security Committee.
record.q: Attorney General Charity Clark today announced she has been appointed co-chair of the National Association of Attorneys General’s (NAAG’s) “Artificial Intelligence (AI) , Internet Safety, Cyber Privacy and Security Committee.”
